html:
The Gilbert and Ellice Islands were a British protectorate from 1892 and a colony from 1916, covering today's Kiribati and Tuvalu. It was run from Tarawa and, for a time, from Banaba.

Britain's main interest was the phosphate of Banaba, mined from 1900, which paid for the colony while ruining the island; see Banabans moved to Rabi. Colonial rule also brought schools and churches to scattered atolls.

The Ellice Islands voted to separate in 1974 and became Tuvalu. The Gilberts became independent as Kiribati on 12 July 1979, under Ieremia Tabai. The Battle of Tarawa was fought here in 1943.
